entry.dc:creator: Miller R.P.
entry.dc:description: See previous abstract

entry.dc:title: Surface mine spoil stability evaluation, interior coal province. Volume 1 - Main report. Glossary of terms (Appendix A) and annotated bibliography (Appendix B).
entry.dc:creator: Miller R.P.
entry.dc:description: This 2-volume report addresses slope stability of surface mine spoils within the interior coal province. 16 mines were visited, pertinent data and samples were collected, and reported spoil instabilities were back-analyzed. Laboratory test results are compared to back-analyzed material properties. Available metods of slope stability analysis are reviewed and evaluated with respect to application to mine spoil stability evaluation and prediction. - from US Govt Reports Announcements, 24, 1980

entry.dc:title: Classification of coal surface mine soil material for vegetation management and soil water quality. Final report.
entry.dc:creator: Lyle E.S.
entry.dc:description: An Alabama minesoil classification system was developed based on soil texture, soil color value and soil pH. Only five different soil classes were found in this study. However, the classification scheme allows for the inclusion of any minesoil that occurs on the basis of its texture, color value and pH. Limestone and fertilizer recommendations are given for soils of the five minesoil classes. - from US Govt. Reports Announcements, 25, 1979

entry.dc:title: Application of satellite data to surface mine monitoring in selected counties of South Carolina. Open file report, (final) Sep 1977-Sep 1978.
entry.dc:creator: Bayne J.
entry.dc:description: Landsat data were used to monitor mining and reclamation activity in several S Carolina mining operations. Differentiation between active-spoil-partially and completely reclaimed areas was successfully demonstrated including small mining operations of less than 30 acres. -from US Govt Reports Announcements, 12, 1980

entry.dc:title: Effect on sediment yield and water quality of a nonrehabilitated surface mine in north-central Wyoming.
entry.dc:creator: Ringen B.H.
entry.prism:publicationName: US Geological Survey Cheyenne Wyoming Water Resources Division Water Resources Investigations
entry.dc:description: Sediment and chemical quality of water data were collected from two adjacent drainage basins in northern Wyoming to compare hydrologic differences between an undisturbed basin and a surface-mined, virtually unrehabilitated basin. Rate of sediment accumulation in a pond in the basin that was surface mined for coal and left unrehabilitated was over 11 times greater than in a pond in the adjacent unmined basin. Sediment yield was a better indicator of the effects of disturbance on mined areas than chemical quality of water. -from US Govt Reports Announcements, 26, 1979

entry.dc:title: Producing black locust biomass for fuel on southern Appalachian surface mines.
entry.dc:creator: Carpenter S.B.
entry.dc:description: For many yrs black locust (Robinia pseudoacacia L.) has been planted extensively in surface mine reclamation across the southern Appalachian region. This tree species has little commercial value but has excellent potential as an alternative fuel resource because of its very high heat equivalent. The fuel plantation concept may be economically feasible on sites where site preparation and planting are part of the surface mine reclamation process. -Authors

entry.dc:title: COKE RECLAIMING PAYS OFF.
entry.dc:creator: Burger J.R.
entry.dc:description: This article describes Pittsburgh Coal & Coke's low-cost reclaiming operation that produces a coke product worth considerably more than washed coal. The company's plant is reclaiming coke from refuse produced by the abandoned beehive coke ovens. In about five years, when the company's several million tons of refuse reserves are used up, the plant will be used to wash coal from a surface mine expected to be opened by that time.

entry.dc:title: CLEARING THE WAY TO FASTER HAULAGE.
entry.dc:creator: Amos E.
entry.dc:description: The author explains how a little known but common chemical can help surface mine and coal handling plant operators keep going in tough winter weather. Calcium chloride combined with salt and abrasives can solve the problems of frozen haulage roads that slow down equipment, cause transportation accidents and often reduce production to below the target rate. In addition to its role as a road de-icer, CaCl//2 can also control dust on haulage roads in summer - a point that's significant in consideration of bulk purchases for year-round use.

entry.dc:title: DRAGLINES CAN REDUCE SURFACE MINING COSTS.
entry.dc:creator: Morey P.
entry.dc:description: Draglines are often the most effective way to surface mine coal. This article briefly explains how to develop dragline stripping mine designs that use the dragline in the most efficient and economic way. Dragline production simulation is also considered.

entry.dc:title: REINFORCED EARTH SPEEDS SURFACE MINE CONSTRUCTION.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: A simple construction system that derives its internal stability from galvanized steel or aluminum straps buried in backfill is finding mine applications, ranging from rock crusher headwalls to massive slot coal storage facilities. Reinforced earth is 20-50 per cent less expensive than alternative earth embankment structures and, compared with cast-in-place concrete walls, six to seven times faster to erect. While the majority of applications are in civil engineering - projects such as retaining walls, bridge abutments, slide buttresses and containment dykes - a growing proportion is mine-related.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MINING REGULATIONS AND LITIGATION FOR 1978.
entry.dc:creator: Todd D.
entry.dc:description: This article covers the regulatory and litigation activities during 1978 regarding the Surface Mine Control and Reclamation Act and the regulations issued thereunder.

entry.dc:title: STRIP MINE RECLAMATION AND REMOTE SENSING TECHNOLOGY.
entry.dc:creator: Brumbaugh F.
entry.dc:description: Remote sensing technology, primarily aerial photography, can be a management tool for many existing as well as future surface mine reclamation needs.

entry.dc:title: THEY SELL 'ALL BUT THE SQUEAL' AT WATERLOO.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: That old saying about using everything from the pig but the squeal has a modern sequel in the coal mining business. Waterloo Coal Co. 's Ohio surface mine operation adds to profitability by selling timber, fireclay, limestone and even some of the shale from the stripped land. This article briefly describes the procedures involved in the removal of these materials, part of which is sold and part of which is utilized by this producer of high-Btu bituminous coal in the reclamation of stripped mine land.

entry.dc:title: Mineral resources and land-use planning, the Watkins, Colorado case: a workshop synopsis.
entry.dc:creator: Lafevers J.
entry.dc:description: The reclamation and land use planning, program, which provides guidance materials and technical services to mining industry and public sector planners concerned with planning for effective land use in surface mine areas, is described. The program integrates reclamation planning with land use planning to assure maximum benefits to the public from both the reuse of mined areas and the efficient utilization of surface resources. Issues of critical importance relating to the potential development of lignite deposits in the vicinity of Denver, Colorado are discussed in detail. -from STAR, 18(1) 1980

entry.dc:title: Mined land reclamation.
entry.dc:creator: Curtis W.R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Energy Environment III Proc 3rd National Conference on the Interagency Energy Environment R and D Program Washington Dc 1 2 June 1978 US Environmental Protection Agency Washington Dc Vitro Lab Division
entry.dc:description: Vegetation can be successfully established on most surface mine spoils if proper mining and reclamation techniques are employed. Such factors and the technology which brings them about, along with the legislative aspects of controlling the technology, are discussed. -from STAR, 17(9), 1979

entry.dc:title: Surface mine reclamation the western way
entry.dc:creator: Schuhart A.

entry.dc:title: HYDRAULIC EXCAVATORS - 1. NEW EXCAVATORS FIND MARKET IN COAL.
entry.dc:creator: Merritt P.
entry.dc:description: Surface mine operators are exploring applications of the hydraulic excavator, a relatively low cost, mobile, track-mounted, diesel-driven unit capable of doing heavy-duty, high production digging in both coal and overburden. Available in both front shovel and backhoe configurations, the hydraulic excavator is competing for a market shared by large capacity wheel loaders and cable shovels in the 10-yd-and-under sizes. One attraction is their ability to mine overburden strata selectively in a standing bulk.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE RECLAMATION SITUATIONS AND PRACTICES ON COAL EXPLORATION AND SURFACE MINE SITES AT SPARWOOD, B. C.
entry.dc:creator: Berdusco R.
entry.dc:description: Kaiser Resources Ltd. owns and operates a 5-million-ton-per-year open-pit and hydraulic coal mine near Sparwood in southeastern British Columbia. Since 1969, Kaiser has maintained a field-scale reclamation program dedicated to the reclamation of disturbances associated with past and present mining and exploration activities. Since that time, over 1400 acres have been treated using modified forestry and agricultural techniques with encouraging results. Both the mining and exploration methods used by the company are described and some reclamation problems encountered are considered.

entry.dc:title: ECONOMIC EVALUATION OF WASHED COAL FOR THE FOUR CORNERS GENERATING STATION.
entry.dc:creator: Suydam C.
entry.dc:description: The potential for upgrading steam coal, by washing in a new coal preparation plant, is considered for an existing surface mine that provides coal to a nearby power plant. The study encompasses three important areas: coal preparation cost and increased mining cost; coal handling and utilization costs in the boiler island equipment; and emission control costs. Results show that proposed coal washing is not economically feasible. Moreover, it points out a pitfall - enrichment of sodium oxide by coal washing that will cause more slagging and fouling in boilers.

entry.dc:title: SIMULATED DEWATERING REQUIREMENTS AT AN OIL SHALE SURFACE MINE, PICEANCE CREEK BASIN, COLORADO.
entry.dc:creator: Banks C.
entry.prism:publicationName: Colo Sch Mines Miner Ind Bull
entry.dc:description: The hydrology modeling described here was performed as support work for a larger study which investigated 10 potential mining cases in the Piceance Creek basin and presented mine designs, engineering and environmental plans and cost estimates for all 10 cases. Nine of the cases were predicted on three different oil shale cutoff grades at three different ore production levels. Major emphasis was placed on approximating dewatering requirements for 1. 25 million tons/day, 15 gallons/ton case at a pit size of about 1. 5 by 2. 75 miles. Results from this base case were then used to approximate dewatering requirements for the larger and smaller pits in all other cases.

entry.dc:title: COAL MINE SUBSIDENCE NEAR SHERIDAN, WYOMING.
entry.dc:creator: Dunrud C.R.
entry.dc:description: Studies of coal mine subsidence features in a 30-sq mi area 3-12 mi north of Sheridan, Wyo, indicate that the long-range surface effects of mining thick coal beds underground beneath weak overburden less than about 200 ft thick are greater than the effects of well-planned surface mining practices with proper reclamation and revegetation. Coal resource recovery also is higher and more efficient in most surface mining operations. Subsidence depressions, cracks, pits, and troughs above underground mine workings can render the surface unusuable for development because of the hazard to people and structures. Fires may start by spontaneous ignition in abandoned coal mines if air and water under the right conditions reach surface mine highwalls or underground workings through subsidence cracks, pits, or troughs.

entry.dc:title: MEXICO PLANS COAL EXPANSION.
entry.dc:creator: Arble M.
entry.dc:description: Despite massive discoveries of oil and gas, Mexico is increasing coal production for domestic use. This artaicle focuses on the country's most important coal expansion which will feed a 1200-Mw thermoelectrical power plant now under construction in the northeast state of Coahuila near the Texas borer. The expansion calls for two deep mines which will produce 6000 mtpd each along with a surface mine producing 2400 mtpd to maintain a 12,000-mtpd total.

entry.dc:title: HOW TO BUILD BETTER HAUL ROADS.
entry.dc:creator: Chironis N.
entry.dc:description: The author discusses the planning and the construction of haul roads, emphasizing that surface mine operators who avoid placing subbase materials under the haul-road surface in the interest of economy are often faced with more costly operation. A variety of construction parameters that must be considered if the haul road is going to hold up under traffic planned for it are discussed. These include subbase and surface materials, thicknesses, road-adhesion characteristics, bearing capacity of soils, and hauling widths.

entry.dc:title: Guidance for land improvement using dredged material.
entry.dc:creator: Spaine P.
entry.dc:description: The report describes techniques for land improvement which utilize dredged material productively as alternatives to conventional disposal methods in regions where land acquisition is difficult and open-water disposal not feasible. Environmental, technical, economic, social and legal aspects of projects are presented as well as outlines of project planning procedures and dredged material transport systems. Three dredged material land improvement techniques are detailed; surface mine reclamation, sanitary landfill and agricultural use. (from Author's, summary)

entry.dc:title: Über eine als Gastropodenlaich gedeutete Eiablage in einer Schale von Pseudopecten aus dem Lias von Salzgitter
entry.dc:creator: Kaiser P.
entry.dc:description: An internal impression of the right valve of Pseudopecten aequivalvis (Sow.) from the Domerium layer (= Lias δ) at a discontinued iron-ore surface mine, Haverlahwiese near Salzgitter, contains bowl-shaped structures which may be interpreted as gastropod spawn. These are compared with similarly formed half-spheres of recent gastropod eggs which are laid on the inner side of a pecten shell. © 1977 E. Schweizerbart'sche Verlagsbuchhandlung.
